endpoints.description: This index.
Every published mission, summarized.
One mission in the mission-timeline/v1 format.
The mission day by day: deadlines, blocks and Plan B groups in order.
What's happening now. Query: at (ISO time, default now), tz (default the mission's).
All missions as one export file the web and iOS apps can import.
Starter templates.
A template built into a mission. Query: from (YYYY-MM-DD, default today), tz.
The iOS app's update feed: { version, notes, url }.
Whether sign-in is set up, and the Google client IDs the apps should use.
Sign in with a Google ID token: { idToken } -> { token, expiresAt, account }.
Sign out on every device. Needs a session token.
Your account. Needs a session token.
Your missions: { revision, updatedAt, missions, tombstones }. Needs a session token.
Save your missions: { baseRevision, missions, tombstones }. 409 with the current state if it changed since baseRevision.
Staff: who you are and your role. 403 if you're not on the staff list.
Staff: customer cases, filtered by ?status=&assignee=&priority=&q=&open=1, with counts per stage.
Staff: open a case { customer: { name, email, phone }, trip, priority, assignee }.
Staff: a case with its notes, history and itineraries.
Staff: change status, priority, assignee, customer or trip. Send baseRevision to avoid overwriting someone else's change (409).
Staff: add an internal note { text }.
Staff: add an itinerary { mission } in the mission-timeline/v1 mission shape.
Staff: replace an itinerary's mission. Shared ones update in the customer's app.
Staff: { shared: true } to send it to the customer's app (by their email), false to take it back.
Staff: the staff list. Admins change it with PUT/DELETE /studio/staff/{email}.
The travel-survey questionnaire: opens a New inquiry case (or updates this email's early one). Public, rate-limited.
Staff: start an itinerary from one of the route ideas for the case's questionnaire.
Customers: trips your studio shared with your email.
Customers: your done / changed / skipped marks and debrief notes { blocks, memos }; the studio sees them.
